key_insight: A scene’s appearance alone may not reveal how it will move. PhysiCalWorld proposes in-context physics calibration to help world models account for hidden physical properties rather than rely on typical training-set behavior.
problem_solved: World models using a single frame or short observation history can miss factors such as mass distribution, joint damping, and surface friction, causing inaccurate predictions and severe drift in unfamiliar scenes.
method: Proposes in-context physics calibration for world models.
Targets hidden physical factors that influence how scenes evolve over time.
The supplied abstract is truncated, so the calibration procedure and evaluation details are unavailable.
impact: Physics-aware calibration could make world-model predictions more reliable in unfamiliar environments. This is potentially useful for simulation and robotic planning, though the supplied excerpt does not establish measured improvements.
visual_elements: Identical-looking objects with different mass distributions or surface friction, producing different motions.
A pipeline diagram: scene observations → physics calibration → world-model prediction.
A conceptual trajectory comparison showing prior-driven drift versus a physics-calibrated prediction, labeled as illustrative.
Icons representing mass distribution, joint damping, and surface friction.
paper_title: PhysiCalWorld: In-Context Physics Calibration for World Models
paper_authors: Yunhao Luo, Wentao He, Yinpei Dai, Hyelin Nam, Hongze Fu
